current_example.problem:
Find the sum modulo $20$ of the solutions to the congruence $8x \equiv 4 \:(\text{mod}\:20).$ 

*Hint: You may wish to use trial and error to find the appropriate multiplicative inverse.*
current_example.worked_solution:
In the given congruence, we have $a=8$ and $n=20,$ so

$$
\text{gcd}(a,n)=\text{gcd}(8,20)=4.
$$

Since $b=4$ is divisible by $4,$ our congruence has $4$ solutions.

First, we reduce the congruence using the division property of congruences:

$$
\begin{aligned}8x & ≡4 &  & (\text{mod}\,20) \\ 4\cdot 2x & ≡4\cdot 1 &  & (\text{mod}\,4\cdot 5) \\ \cancel{4}\cdot 2x & ≡\cancel{4}\cdot 1 &  & (\text{mod}\,\cancel{4}\cdot 5) \\ 2x & ≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,5)\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that in the new congruence, we have $a_1=2$ and $n_1=5,$ so

$$
\text{gcd}(a_1,n_1)=\text{gcd}(2,5)=1.
$$

This means our congruence has a unique solution modulo $5.$

To find the solution, we need to multiply both sides of the equation by the multiplicative inverse of $2\,(\textrm{mod}\:5).$ To find the inverse of $2\,(\textrm{mod}\:5),$ we compute the exponents of $2\,(\textrm{mod}\:5)$ until we get a result of $1 \,(\textrm{mod}\:5)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{2}^{2} & ≡4 &  & (\text{mod}\,5) \\ {2}^{3} & ≡4\cdot 2≡8≡1\cdot 5+3≡3 &  & (\text{mod}\,5) \\ {2}^{4} & ≡3\cdot 2≡6≡1\cdot 5+1≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,5)\end{aligned}
$$

So, $2 \cdot 3 \equiv 1 \:(\textrm{mod}\:5),$ which means that $3$ is the multiplicative inverse of $2$ (modulo $5$).

Now, multiplying both sides of our congruence by $3,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x & ≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,5) \\ 3\cdot 2x & ≡3\cdot 1 &  & (\text{mod}\,5) \\ (3\cdot 2)x & ≡3 &  & (\text{mod}\,5) \\ x & ≡3 &  & (\text{mod}\,5)\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get one solution, $x \equiv 3 \: (\text{mod}\:5).$ 

But our original congruence was modulo $20$ (not modulo $5$). To find all the solutions modulo $20,$ we repeatedly add $5$ modulo $20$ until we reach the number $3$ again:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ≡3 &  & (\text{mod}\,20) \\ {x}_{2} & ≡3+5≡8 &  & (\text{mod}\,20) \\ {x}_{3} & ≡8+5≡13 &  & (\text{mod}\,20) \\ {x}_{4} & ≡13+5≡18 &  & (\text{mod}\,20) \\ {x}_{5} & ≡18+5≡23≡1\cdot 20+3≡3≡{x}_{1} &  & (\text{mod}\,20)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $x\equiv 3, 8, 13, 18 \: (\text{mod}\:20).$ 

Finally,

$$
3+8+13+18 \equiv 2 \quad (\text{mod}\:20).
$$
